role: Sole machine-readable authority for the live Elpis system boundary. Every other description (README, docs, build files) is derived from or checked against this file.
purpose: Research direction: geodesic intelligence. Persistent structured state, memory topology, relational structure, bounded transformations, controlled evolution and inference interact so that computation follows structure already accumulated by the system instead of being reconstructed from an unstructured prompt. This is an architectural research direction, not a claim of general intelligence.

shared_modules.role: Canonical content identity v1 (domain-framed canonical JSON SHA-256) used across subsystems.

subsystems.purpose: Machine/OS substrate and memory management below every model: content hashing, FMS residency (HOT/WARM/COLD logical tiers over RAM/device/storage physical domains) with a POSIX platform abstraction layer, Linux descriptor capabilities, sealed native loading, deployment-pinned resource authority and verified file-backed assets materialized on demand into bounded residency; plus the vendor-neutral bounded native execution scheduler and explicit post-compiled accelerator backend port. The base build owns no vendor accelerator SDK or kernel.
subsystems.mutation_authority: The substrate never mutates admitted external assets (no writable replicas). It owns only its own residency state: page registration, leases and eviction inside configured budgets. Admission requires a deployment-pinned catalog; inspection never creates authority.
subsystems.runtime_participation: Constructed by the runtime composition when file-backed memory is configured; consumed by inference (associative rows, experts, prefetch).
subsystems.security_boundary: Trusted root selected once; opens resolve beneath its descriptor with openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS; native code is copied into a sealed memfd, digest-verified, then loaded. Linux only; other platforms fail closed.
subsystems.maturity: Mechanics qualified: native FMS invariant/concurrency/adversarial suites, Python admission/lease/eviction/adversarial path suites, the native file-asset page service (elpis_fms_file_service: transferred read-only descriptors, native page verification, FMS leases and LRU eviction differentially equal to FMSFileAssets), and bounded execution scheduling with opportunistic PURE backend fallback plus terminal BACKEND_ONLY provider-stream semantics.
incomplete_interfaces: COLD tier for file assets is external immutable storage only; no writable cold replica is implemented.
Buffered pread accounting does not charge or bound the Linux page cache.
No accelerator/device fences on the CPU POSIX PAL (bind_fence fails closed).

subsystems.purpose: Persistent identity, continuity and history: deterministic entities and lifecycle, sender-bound local messaging, deterministic scheduling, one authoritative durable event history, canonical state roots, replay, checkpoints, crash recovery, read-only topology and context projections, and the frozen Structural R0 mutation grammar.
subsystems.mutation_authority: Only Kernel transitions (found/activate/dormant/terminate/message/step) mutate ECS state, each linearized under the kernel lock and committed as one framed event before the projection is installed. Projections (topology, context) are read-only. Entity-facing code sends only through kernel-bound EntityPort objects and cannot choose its sender.
subsystems.runtime_participation: The runtime composition owns one Kernel as the system's durable history; receipts of other subsystems are recorded there as messages. Projections feed inference context read-only.
subsystems.persistence: Length-framed append-only event log with fsync durability boundary and complete-frame crash recovery; checkpoints are rollback-floor markers only.
subsystems.maturity: Mechanics qualified in-process (same-process POSIX model). No cross-process transport or authority.
incomplete_interfaces: Structural R0 mutations are executable and verified but not admitted as kernel transitions.
Cross-process transport, federation and cross-process authority are deferred.

subsystems.purpose: Geometric world-model subsystem. G0 materializes the frozen microscopic cubic ECS mathematics; G1 adds an owned microscopic world state W and the exact deterministic full-batch cubic gradient recurrence inherited from the qualified Branch36 dynamical regime. S3=(mu,M,T3) remains a derived raw-sum macrostate; W remains authoritative.
subsystems.mutation_authority: G1 may mutate only its own in-memory microscopic W through the explicit atomic cubic full-batch gradient step. Candidate W' is fully computed and finite-validated before installation; rejection leaves W and epoch unchanged. No ECS_C, HACF, inference, canonical or filesystem state may be mutated.
subsystems.runtime_participation: NONE at G1. The stateful recurrence is qualified as an ECS_G primitive but no DSV4.1 observation adapter or runtime composition invokes it yet.
subsystems.security_boundary: Native state owns only finite binary64 W and an epoch counter. Step scratch is caller-owned. No filesystem, network, model invocation, ECS_C/HACF access, background threads or retained external pointers.
subsystems.maturity: G1 stateful recurrence candidate: G0 cubic/S3 arithmetic plus an owned microscopic state and atomic full-batch gradient transition. Differential qualification targets the exact d=6, N in {36,48,72}, no-width-normalization regime; runtime observation semantics remain unadmitted.
incomplete_interfaces: No DSV4.1-to-ECS_G observation contract is defined or admitted.
No ECS_G-to-DSV4.1 projection transport is wired.
No runtime composition invokes ECS_G yet.
No durable ECS_G snapshot/persistence contract is admitted; ECS_C remains the continuity/history subsystem.

subsystems.mutation_authority: Structural memory is written only by its owner (corpus ingestion into a caller-owned state root). Retrieval, validation, views, topology and observations are read-only and grant no semantic truth, execution or admission authority. Canonical Grid81 state is read here but changed only by the pipeline's canonical writer path.
subsystems.runtime_participation: The runtime composition may own a HACF corpus/index; retrieval results become evidence envelopes consumable by the pipeline, the ECS history and inference structural proposals.

Chunk resolution verifies document bytes and recomputes the elpis-chunk-v1 identity but does not re-derive the chunker's segmentation (the native chunker is not exposed to Python): a self-consistent claim over a sub-range of a real document resolves to that document's own verified bytes.

subsystems.purpose: Two paths. (1) Bounded ingress: a streaming Regex lexer over a bounded interval-specification grammar -> read-only HACF lexical retrieval and one-hop context graph -> a zero-authority context proposal -> an atomic query-local proposal batch published as a semantic query overlay; ambiguity rejects before any batch. (2) The canonical Grid81 writer pipeline, one authority boundary per stage: deterministic structural adjudication -> capability authority decision and one granted-unconsumed structural-influence capability -> capability consumption into an inert artifact -> application against shadow capability state with a durable SQLite application ledger -> read-only advisory promotion plan -> promotion authority (explicit operator approval, one-use capability) -> isolated successor candidate -> atomic publication (durable publication ledger reservation, renameat2 exchange, post-commit verification through the canonical reader).
subsystems.mutation_authority: Ingress mutates nothing: it opens an existing HACF corpus, performs only lexical reads and never creates one, and every result carries zero semantic, admission, execution and runtime authority. Only elpis.pipeline.canonical.publisher changes canonical Grid81 state, and only with the exact one-use promotion capability object issued by elpis.pipeline.canonical.authority against an explicit operator approval digest. Adjudication, capability evaluation and promotion planning are read-only; consumption and application write only caller-owned shadow state and ledgers.
subsystems.runtime_participation: The runtime composition may run ingress on caller-supplied bytes against a corpus it owns and hand the proposal export to inference (structural address proposals); it may drive the writer stages in process. Nothing runs implicitly, and each stage consumes only the previous stage's typed output.
subsystems.security_boundary: Ingress takes bytes, never paths to read; the bounded lexer refuses input beyond its carry profile before any evidence is built; the bridge library is loaded only from an explicit path, exports only its declared ABI (linker version script) and refuses symlinked, relative or absent corpus roots. The Python binding re-reads the four authority flags and refuses any result that claims authority. Fail closed at every stage: proposals and model output are never authority; the promotion plan is advisory and non-executable; the one-use promotion capability binds the source canonical digest and generation it was issued against, and the publisher re-reads the canonical root under an exclusive flock on its Canonical parent and refuses any other state, symlinked layout, or candidate inside the root; publication reserves a durable ledger entry, exchanges atomically with renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE) and verifies through the production reader; replay is idempotent and a consumed capability cannot be reused. Linux only.

subsystems.purpose: Generic, deterministic evolution: canonical integer genotypes, bounded mutation seeded from content-addressed lineage, persistent organisms with a lifecycle law, atomic energy-conserving reproduction, exact integer fitness, self-verified truncation selection over a population revision, an evolution path gate that admits one bounded attempt per exact ECS-history-bound assertion and chains transition receipts, and evaluation-gated promotion of a candidate workspace over its incumbent with atomic materialization.
subsystems.mutation_authority: Evolution records are immutable values; every state change returns a new population, organism or receipt and nothing is written in place. Selection and reproduction commit only against the exact revision the caller observed and reject atomically otherwise. Promotion writes a child workspace only at a caller-supplied, not-yet-existing destination, and only when its content matches the selected manifest. The path gate grants no authority beyond the single attempt it admits.
subsystems.runtime_participation: The runtime composition may run gated evolution attempts against an ECS projection of its own history and record their transition receipts in that history.
subsystems.security_boundary: No implicit randomness (mutation seeds derive from lineage content), no model, no numerics, no network. Selection accepts no externally proposed solution and recomputes every fitness score. The path gate type-checks the history projection and executes nothing for a rejected assertion. Promotion refuses symlinks and special files in workspaces and edit paths outside the child.

subsystems.purpose: Inference behind contracts, driver-neutral: typed target records (tensors, latent inputs, target state, step receipts) and a Target protocol a driver implements; n-gram associative addressing (DSV4.1 engram and Qwen PLE schemes) with bounded row lookup over substrate file assets; immutable context lifetimes/snapshots and sparse global candidate selection; digest-bound experts executed from file assets; physical prefetch predictions that can never select content; the structural address-proposal edge contract (inference never parses or validates slow-lane artifacts; the adapters live in elpis.runtime.edges); an atomic, replay-verified decode transaction; speculative drafting verified token by token by the target (greedy equivalence); a read-only observer over completed decode epochs with future-only latent steering applied through the target's own latent-input path. The first driver is DSV4 (drivers/dsv4: a compact target and an explicit synthetic fixture intake). Token streaming is a separate fast lane: sequence transactions (begin, then next per token, then finalize) validate committed input once, run only model arithmetic per token with no canonical or provenance identity and no re-hashing of admitted bytes, and build receipts, identities and the committed state at the finalization boundary, identical to the legacy transaction's. HACF, not KV, is the context substrate: the principal path (elpis.inference.principal) takes context only as a ContextAdmission (admitted HACF objects rendered to input tokens under an explicit object/byte/token budget, frozen for one sequence) and keeps keys/values only as bounded, ephemeral attention scratch (at most local_window entries) inside one sequence; its committed PrincipalState holds no K/V, compressed pool, global index or token history and does not grow with stored or attended context. The legacy transaction, the legacy-identical sequence path and their NeuralState/compressed-KV/G-X identities remain for historical replay only. A separate digest-bound DeepSeek recipe V4.1 text adapter encodes text/chat and incrementally decodes new token bytes with at most three carry bytes; tokenizer loading and encoding occur before begin. Read-only safetensors preflight inventories pinned artifacts but cannot instantiate a production driver.
subsystems.mutation_authority: Only InferenceEngine.execute commits decode state, and only as one transaction against the exact expected state; a failed step commits nothing and replay re-executes the receipt chain to validate history. Every proposal record (address proposals, drafts, prefetch plans, steering observations/proposals/applications) is ProposalOnly with fixed zero semantic, admission, execution and mutation authority. Steering never mutates weights, context, tokens or logits: its only effect is one LatentInput on a later request, recorded by the transaction. Inference never writes ECS, structural memory or canonical state; model output is proposal, never authority. On the sequence path inputs are turn-scoped: a GREEDY continuation must carry exactly the running turn's latents and proposals, so slow-lane results (steering latents, structural proposals) enter only on a PREFILL turn boundary, never mid-trajectory.
subsystems.runtime_participation: The runtime composition constructs a driver target from explicitly supplied file assets (tests use the synthetic DSV4 fixture), passes structural address proposals from ingress or retrieval, runs decode transactions, and records their receipt digests in the ECS history.
subsystems.security_boundary: No network, no downloads and no implicit model: a target exists only from caller-supplied, digest-verified file assets registered through elpis.substrate beneath its trusted root, and every bank, expert, parameter artifact and projection is bound to the target's model identity. Prefetch predicts physical ranges only and cannot change which rows are read. Proposals arrive as already validated, digest-pinned AddressProposal values and are checked against the snapshot they are bound to. elpis.inference imports no ECS, structure, pipeline, evolution or runtime module, directly or transitively (boundary-tested). Fixed IEEE-754 binary64 arithmetic in steering; no hidden or global mutable recurrence state.

The NumPy F32 implementation remains the architectural reference; the sealed CPU-native backend is qualified against it, while vendor accelerator implementations remain external to the base build and must enter through the substrate acceleration port. Above the unchanged generic execution port, the YTS-R0 provider stream (docs/inference/DSV41_PROVIDER_STREAM.md), Native Clock R0 and Native Materializer R1 (docs/inference/DSV41_NATIVE_CLOCK.md) are qualified with the test-only CPU reference provider: one native clock_advance runs prefill and generation, and with the sealed production materializer (elpis_dsv41_materializer) file-backed Engram row decoding, page verification, FMS leases and expert-range staging execute natively with zero Python callbacks, bitwise equal to the Python YTS/RowEngine/TensorStore/FMSFileAssets oracle, which remains.

Speculative verification is greedy-equivalence only; no sampling-equivalent acceptance rule.

Sequence begin still validates the committed lineage with the legacy validator, which walks the whole receipt history before its validated-state cache check; this is paid once per sequence, not per token.
The legacy per-token transaction (InferenceEngine.execute) still computes identities on every token; it remains the replay oracle and is not the streaming path.
Speculative decoding and physical prefetch are not on the sequence lane yet; they run only through the legacy transaction.

Retiring or re-scoping the channel-X contract is pending.
V4.1 text chat only; tool/image templates and model-specific stop extensions are unsupported. Full recipe framework integration is not imported.

The principal path's attention reach is the local window (the fixture's local_window is 4): admitted context influences generation through that window and the model-owned associative rows, not through a KV pool. It is intentionally not numerically equivalent to the legacy compressed-KV kernel; the difference is exactly the global compressed-KV term.
Prefill re-reads admitted context every turn: reconstruction cost replaces resident KV memory and is measured by tests/integration/context_scaling_benchmark.py.

subsystems.purpose: The one runtime composition: Runtime wires the subsystems explicitly around one durable receipt history (ReceiptHistory), an ECS kernel history founded with one history entity and one recorder entity per subsystem. It runs one subsystem operation at a time through that subsystem's own fail-closed entry point (pipeline ingress, structure retrieval-bundle admission, canonical Grid81 publication, the evolution path gate bound to a projection of the runtime's own history, and one inference decode transaction) and records the committed outcome as a kernel-attributed message. It owns the edge adapters (elpis.runtime.edges) that turn ingress exports and retrieval bundles into inference AddressProposals before a sequence begins. It composes the context-substrate path explicitly (admit_context: ingress -> edge adapter -> HACF object resolution -> ContextAdmission, recorded; run_principal: begin -> streamed tokens -> finalize, commit recorded) with nothing running during the token loop. It is not a numbered runtime generation. run_text renders and encodes chat before begin, streams incremental text alongside token emission, and records principal.commit then an inert text.output digest after finalization. No generated text is admitted as memory.
subsystems.mutation_authority: The runtime writes only its own ECS receipt history, and only through ReceiptHistory.record: one message from the owning subsystem's recorder entity to the history entity, appended only after that subsystem's own operation committed or published. Recording is idempotent and grants the recorded thing no authority. Every other state change (canonical publication, decode state, evolution receipts) is made by the owning subsystem's entry point with the caller's explicit inputs; the runtime adds no authority and no fallback.
subsystems.security_boundary: The history directory is an explicit absolute path and the history is replay-validated on open (event chain, clock progression, state roots); a history founded with other entities, a record sent by the wrong recorder, or a non-canonical record payload is refused. Libraries, corpus roots, file assets, ledgers and promotion capabilities are supplied explicitly by the caller; the runtime opens no network connection and loads no model. The evolution gate receives a projection taken at call time, so an assertion bound to an older history head is rejected before anything executes.
protocol_identifiers_retained: New: elpis.runtime.history.v1 (history genesis label), elpis.runtime.receipt-record.v1 (record payload schema). The ECS identifiers it builds on (ecs.event.v1, ecs.message.v1, ecs.state_root.v3) are owned by elpis.ECS_C.
subsystems.model_dependency: NONE_REQUIRED. Inference runs only on caller-supplied targets; the integration suite uses the synthetic DSV4 fixture.
subsystems.maturity: Integration qualified: five end-to-end suites over real native libraries and a real HACF corpus (ingress, structural memory, canonical writer, evolution, inference with the DSV4 fixture), including record idempotence, replay on reopen, tamper refusal, stale-history rejection and non-recording of refused operations.
incomplete_interfaces: Ingress proposals are recorded but the query-local overlay itself is not persisted; recording carries its identity only.
Steering epochs (steering.global_event_fields) are not yet recorded; the steered engine is composed by the caller, not by Runtime.
Canonical publication is recorded after the fact; the application and promotion stages before it are driven by the caller and not recorded.
The runtime is single-process and same-process like the ECS kernel; no cross-process transport or service boundary.
record() re-reads the event log after each write; adequate at test scale, not an indexed store.
Sequence outputs are committed and recorded but not yet written back into HACF, so the next turn's retrieval does not yet see the previous turn's output unless the caller ingests it.

The only Python-reachable HACF builder is the retrieval bridge, which indexes at most 64 documents and 128 chunks; context-scaling measurements stay inside that ceiling although ingress and resolution open corpora of any size.

Text transport is qualified with a scripted emission double only. Canonical ECS-to-HACF/context projection and explicit post-sequence generated-content admission remain separate edges; caller supplies the context snapshot.
